subject.title: refactor(memory-wiki): move compiled cache to plugin state

question: Should OpenClaw expose `registerMemoryPromptPreparation` as a permanent general plugin-SDK contract, or keep asynchronous compiled-cache loading behind a narrower owner-specific seam?
rationale: The diff adds a new public plugin API whose lifecycle and compatibility expectations extend beyond Memory Wiki; tests cannot determine the intended long-term SDK boundary.

options.title: Approve a narrow public SDK hook
options.body: Retain the registration after documenting its ordering, error, snapshot, and compatibility guarantees and resolving the digest-only prompt-read concern.

options.title: Keep the behavior owner-private
options.body: Replace the public registration with a Memory Wiki-specific integration until another plugin demonstrates the same requirement.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow public SDK hook
recommendation.body: Retain the registration after documenting its ordering, error, snapshot, and compatibility guarantees and resolving the digest-only prompt-read concern.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied feature history identifies this contributor as the active author of the proposed cross-plugin contract and Memory Wiki lifecycle design.
